result.title: Do Waste Classifiers Recognise Items They Have Never Seen? Object-Disjoint Evaluation on Household and Medical Waste
result.summary: Automatic waste classification supports source separation, which enables recycling and keeps hazardous medical items out of household waste. Waste classification studies often report near-perfect accuracy on random image splits, which put photographs of one item in both training and test sets. To measure how well classifiers recognise items they have never seen, we built BanglaWaste-23, with 4,160 images of 172 objects in 23 household and medical waste classes from Bangladesh. Every image also records which physical item it shows. We evaluated 11 ImageNet-pretrained models and two models trained from scratch (a compact custom network and MobileNetV3-L) using object-disjoint five-fold cross-validation and a random split. On unseen objects, the best pretrained model reached a macro-averaged F1 score of 98.8%, and six models were statistically tied. The random split overstated from-scratch accuracy by 15 to 19 percentage points. The from-scratch models also missed 11 to 13% of medical items, against under 1% for pretrained models. On a second dataset from Dhaka, pretrained accuracy fell by 15 to 22 points. Classifiers should therefore be evaluated on unseen objects, with random-split results read as an upper bound. The data are on Zenodo and the code at https://github.com/saadbaust/BanglaWaste-23.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文构建了含 172 件实体物品的孟加拉国垃圾分类数据集 BanglaWaste-23，并用「对象不重叠」划分评估 11 个 ImageNet 预训练模型与两个从头训练模型，指出随机划分会高估准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究内容是垃圾分类的图像分类评测协议，未涉及视觉语言模型内部状态、推理生成或证据使用，与 LVR 主线无实质联系；对象不重叠划分虽有评测思路，但缺乏可迁移到 latent 推理的具体线索。
